title: Machine for Testing Record Validity
statement: For every natural number $k$ and finite decidable types $Q,T$, there are a natural number $K$, a finite decidable state type $P$, a deterministic machine $R$ with $K+2$ work tapes over the record alphabet, entry and distinct yes/no states, and a constant $C$ with the following property. For any natural numbers $n,s$, list of fields $f$ of length $k+3$, and entry-state configuration $d$ whose tape $0$ encodes $f$, tape $1$ encodes the prescribed template for $n,s$, and all tapes with index at least $2$ are blank, the machine reaches in at most $C(|\langle f\rangle|+|\langle H\rangle|+n+1)$ steps the original configuration with state changed to yes if $f$ encodes a valid record for parameters $k,n,s,Q,T$, and to no otherwise. It visits neither decision state earlier, and through that time every work-tape head moves by at most $C(|\langle f\rangle|+|\langle H\rangle|+1)$ from its initial position, where $H$ is the prescribed template and validity means that $f$ is the record of a configuration on an input of length $n$ whose work-tape heads and nonblank cells lie within distance $s$ of the origin.
hypotheses_covered: Tape $1$ encodes the prescribed template for $n,s$
All tapes with index at least $2$ are blank
